source.label: Placed in NGC 1637 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 9,289,203 pc (src/objects/ngc-1637-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 9,289,664 pc, inclination 31.1 deg, line of nodes 20.6 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Jones2009ApJ...696.1176J: Distance Determination to 12 Type II Supernovae Using the Expanding Photosphere Method (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...696.1176J); catalogue reference Jones2009ApJ...696.1176J: 9289663.8678 pc (-458864.863614/+482708.341758); sn

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color of a blackbody at the star's temperature; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of a blackbody at the star's published temperature. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,770 K and log g 0.65 (u1 0.692, u2 0.086): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention.
